business: SEGMENT: PI car accident intake, Pleasanton (Shotland pilot)
prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but first a few quick questions so I can give a useful recommendation:
- How serious were your injuries (minor, required ER/hospitalization, ongoing treatment)?  
- Was fault disputed, or do you expect the other driver/insurance to deny liability?  
- Any police report or witnesses?  
- Is the other driver insured? Are you using your own insurance (UM/MedPay)?  
- Do you want me to list specific Pleasanton / Bay Area attorneys or give guidance on how to choose one yourself?

General guidance — who to hire
- Look for a personal injury attorney who specializes in car-accident cases (auto collisions). That’s the right practice area.  
- Prefer lawyers who handle mostly injury/auto cases (not generalists) and who have recent experience in Alameda County courts and with local insurers.  
- Choose someone who has trial experience and a proven record of negotiating fair settlements; many cases settle, but you want a lawyer willing to go to trial if needed.  
- Most car-accident lawyers work on contingency (no fee unless they recover money). Typical fees are about 33%–40% plus case costs; confirm exact terms.  

How to vet attorneys (what to check)
- CA State Bar record (status, any discipline).  
- Client reviews and recent settlements/verdicts (look for similar injury types).  
- Ask how long they’ve practiced, how many auto cases they handle per year, and whether they personally handle your file.  
- Ask whether they advance case costs and how those are repaid.  
- Check responsiveness in the initial consult — that often predicts how they’ll communicate during the case.  

Important questions to ask at the first consultation
- Have you handled cases like mine? What was the typical result?  
- Who will handle my case day-to-day (attorney, associate, paralegal)? How will I reach them?  
- What is your fee structure and what costs will I be responsible for?  
- Do you handle cases on a contingency basis? If so, what percentage and how are costs deducted?  
- How long do you expect my case might take? What are the likely next steps?  
- Will you take this case to trial if necessary?  
- Can you provide references from recent clients?  

Important immediate steps for you (do these now if you haven’t)
- Get medical care and follow treatment — medical records are essential to prove injury.  
- Get the police report number and a copy of the report.  
- Preserve evidence: photos of vehicles, scene, injuries; repair estimates; dashcam/cellphone footage.  
- Collect witness names and contact info.  
- Notify your insurance company as required, but be careful: do not give a recorded statement or sign full-release paperwork without talking to an attorney.  
- Don’t post details or photos about the accident/injuries on social media.  
- Be aware of deadlines: in California the general statute of limitations for personal injury is 2 years from the date of the accident (there are exceptions), and claims against government entities have much shorter notice deadlines (often 6 months). If a government vehicle or public property is involved, talk to an attorney right away.  

If you want specific local lawyers
I can pull together a short list of reputable personal injury/auto attorneys in Pleasanton or nearby (Dublin, Livermore, Walnut Creek, San Ramon). Tell me:
- Which city you prefer (Pleasanton or broader East Bay)?  
- Whether you want only attorneys who offer free consultations and represent on contingency?  
- Any other preferences (trial attorney, language, price sensitivity)?

If you prefer to pick yourself, I can also draft an email or phone script you can use for initial consultations. Which would you like to do next?
